h.Resposta curta: a placa é para o ponto p: Short answer: the stand is for the spot every customer passes, like the checkout or front desk. The card is for whoever serves the customer up close, and it travels in their pocket. If your business has both, the norm is to have both.
h.A placa fica em pé no caixa, na mesa ou: The stand sits upright at the checkout, on the table or at the front desk. Its strength is that it's there all the time: the customer sees it while waiting for change, while the card machine processes, while waiting to be called. Sometimes they leave a review without anyone asking.
h.M ou G? A M (10 × 15 cm) cabe em mesa, b: M or L? The M (10 × 15 cm) fits on a table, a narrow counter or a small front desk. The L (21 × 15 cm) is meant to be seen from afar, at the main checkout. If in doubt, the L at the checkout and the M on the tables.
h.O cartão tem o tamanho de um cartão de c: The card is the size of a credit card and stays with the staff member. Its strength is the moment: the staff member finishes the job, the customer compliments them, and the card comes out at the right time, along with a face-to-face request. A personal request at the moment the customer is happy works better than any stand.
h.Um cartão por atendente. Cada cartão é u: One card per staff member. Each card is a separate device in the dashboard, so you can see how many taps each one got. It becomes a simple way to keep track of your team, and to recognize who asks the most.
h.Quase sempre que o negócio tem balcão e: Almost always when the business has a counter and personal service. A restaurant with the stand at the checkout and a card per waiter. A salon with the stand at the front desk and a card per professional. The stand catches those who pass the checkout without being invited. The card catches those who were well served and heard the request.
